mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a C200 CDI typically costs between £600 and £4,800 depending on the engine code and condition. Used OM646 units start from £600-£1,400, reconditioned from £1,800-£3,000, and fully rebuilt OM651 engines from £2,800-£4,800. A replacement OM651.913 engine costs on average £2,797 in good condition, with reconditioned units costing up to £3,295. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: What is 'Black Death' and does it affect the C-Class 200 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: 'Black Death' refers to injector seal failure that affects OM646 engines. The copper washer seal between the injector and cylinder head degrades, allowing combustion gases to escape. This creates hard, black carbon deposits around the injector. Symptoms include a ticking or chuffing noise, a strong diesel smell in the cabin, hissing sounds from the engine, and visible black tar-like residue. If left untreated, the injector can seize in the cylinder head, requiring expensive extraction and head repairs.

mainEntity.name: Does the C-Class 200 CDI have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the engine. The OM646 (W204 C200 CDI, 2007-2009) uses a duplex timing chain at the front of the engine, which is robust and does not require scheduled replacement. The OM651 (W204 C200 CDI BlueEFFICIENCY, 2011-2014) uses a timing chain at the rear of the engine, which is prone to stretching. A metallic rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W204 C200 CDI is typically worth £2,500-£6,000 - a rebuilt OM646 or OM651 engine (£2,200-£4,800) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. For vehicles with lower values, a used engine or targeted repair is often more economical. Always compare the cost of repair against the car's market value.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM646 and OM651 engines in the C200 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM646 is a 2.2-litre diesel used in the W204 C200 CDI (2007-2009) with a front-mounted duplex timing chain and piezo injectors. The OM651 is a 2.1-litre diesel introduced in the W204 C200 CDI BlueEFFICIENCY (2011-2014), featuring a rear-mounted timing chain and 2,000 bar rail pressure. Both produce 136 hp, but the OM651 offers increased torque (360 Nm vs 270 Nm).

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the C200 CDI is most commonly caused by EGR valve clogging, turbocharger issues (sticking variable vanes), or injector seal failure ('Black Death'). On OM651 engines, timing chain stretch can also cause cam timing drift and power loss. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C200 CDI badge has represented the entry-level diesel offering across multiple generations of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class. From the W203 to the W204, the C200 CDI evolved through two distinct engine families - the OM646 and the OM651 - each with different characteristics and failure patterns. The badge served as a popular choice for fleet and economy-focused buyers, offering strong fuel economy with adequate performance.

milestones.description: OM646.963, 2.2L diesel, 122 hp - W203 C200 CDI facelift launch; improved injector design over OM611
OM646.811 EVO, 2.2L diesel, 136 hp (100 kW) - W204 C200 CDI launch; piezo injectors; 270 Nm torque
OM646.812 EVO, 2.2L diesel, 136 hp (100 kW) - W204 C200 CDI variant
OM651.913, 2.1L diesel, 136 hp (100 kW) - W204 C200 CDI BlueEFFICIENCY; Euro 5 emissions; 360 Nm torque
W204 production ends; C200 CDI badge replaced by C200d in W205 generation

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The C200 CDI has been powered by two distinct diesel engine families across the W204 generation - the OM646 and the OM651. The OM646 is renowned for durability with front-mounted duplex timing chains but shares the "Black Death" injector seal failure with earlier engines. The OM651 introduced a rear-mounted timing chain that became the primary replacement driver. Rebuilt C200 CDI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM646 Injector Seal Failure - "Black Death" Carbon Buildup in the C200 CDI
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI (OM646.811 and OM646.812, W204, 2007-2009)
problems.rootCause: The copper washer seal between the injector and cylinder head degrades over time, allowing combustion gases to escape past the seal. The escaping gas mixes with carbon and unburnt fuel, creating hard, black, crusty deposits around the injector - commonly known as "Black Death". Symptoms include a chuffing or ticking noise, a strong diesel smell in the cabin, hissing sounds from the engine, and visible black tar-like residue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove one injector, clean seat, replace copper washer and clamp bolt
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; prevents injector seizure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: All four injector seals replaced, carbon removal from bores, leak-off testing
repairOptions.longevity: For moderate carbon buildup; specialist approach significantly cheaper

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Seized injector drilling/extraction, cylinder head removal, injector bore machining
repairOptions.longevity: Required if injector cannot be extracted non-destructively

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W204 C200 CDI is worth £2,500-£6,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £3,500, a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value - a used engine or targeted injector seal repair is usually more economical. For well-maintained examples, a rebuilt OM646 with warranty can be a worthwhile investment.
problems.recommendation: The "Black Death" is insidious but slow-moving. If you hear a ticking or chuffing noise that changes with engine speed, or smell diesel fumes in the cabin, inspect the injector area immediately. Caught early, an £180-£300 single seal replacement is cheap peace of mind.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM646 Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Failure - Why the W204 BlueEFFICIENCY C200 CDI Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The OM651 uses a timing chain mounted at the rear of the engine, adjacent to the gearbox. The chain stretches over time due to inadequate tensioner design and extended oil change intervals. A metallic rattling or clattering noise on cold start for 2-5 seconds is the classic warning sign. If the chain jumps or snaps, the engine requires cylinder head removal and valve replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioners, guides, and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cylinder head removal, valve replacement, piston inspection, full timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped; bent valves almost certain

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement with professionally rebuilt OM651 unit with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value on higher-mileage cars

problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the rear of the engine on cold starts - especially between 80,000 and 120,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£700-£1,100) saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Once the chain jumps, piston-to-valve contact is almost certain and engine replacement becomes the only viable option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI engine prices

problems.group: OM646 & OM651 EGR Valve & Turbocharger Issues
problems.h4: OM646 & OM651 EGR Valve & Turbocharger Issues
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 200 CDI (OM646.811/812 and OM651.913, W204, 2007-2014)
problems.rootCause: The EGR valve can become clogged with carbon deposits, particularly on vehicles used for short journeys. The variable geometry turbocharger can suffer from sticking vanes due to carbon buildup, causing loss of boost and reduced power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and clean EGR valve; or replace if necessary
repairOptions.longevity: Viable; carbon buildup is the main cause

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace or rebuild turbocharger, oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Required if turbo has failed or vanes are seized

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new turbo and EGR components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If your C200 CDI experiences loss of power, particularly when climbing hills, have the turbocharger and EGR system inspected. A £300-£600 EGR clean or £800-£1,500 turbo repair is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Regular motorway driving helps keep the EGR and turbo vanes clear.
